threats.title: Stolen or replayed Bearer token
threats.description: An attacker reuses a valid or expired JWT obtained through prompt injection or log leakage to call internal REST APIs with the agent’s privileges
threats.mitigation: Use short-lived access tokens (maximum 300 seconds), enable refresh token rotation, validate audience (aud), issuer (iss) and expiry (exp) on every request, and store tokens securely. Reject reused or expired tokens.

threats.title: Over-privileged token returns excessive data
threats.description:
The agent’s access token contains broader scopes than the end-user is entitled to, allowing retrieval of PII or admin-level data.
Threat 3
threats.mitigation: Apply least-privilege scopes. Issue tokens with only the minimum required permissions (e.g. read:ai-data). Perform server-side authorization checks on every API call instead of trusting the token scope alone.

threats.title: Scope escalation to write:admin
threats.description: A compromised or spoofed agent identity obtains the write:admin scope and performs privileged actions on behalf of a normal user
threats.mitigation: Enforce strict scope validation. Never allow an agent to self-elevate privileges. Use separate M2M clients for different privilege levels and bind high-privilege actions to additional controls (e.g. Ed25519 signature verification or human approval).
